Jake — great to connect. Looping in Vanessa, Karthik, and Ben (partner ops / commercial / infra respectively).

Short answers up front:
- We can support tiered retention (hot: 90 days by default, warm: 1 year, cold: custom up to 7 years) with automated lifecycle policies.
- Cold retrieval latency target (S3-backed) is 200–800ms typical for index lookups within our batch fallthrough pattern; SLA can be structured differently if you require <200ms.
- For marketplace bundles that include S3 egress we recommend a blended per-embedding unit that splits egress and compute and a revenue-share floor to cover storage egress.

I’ve attached a first-draft SOW and a proposed ops-level table for comment. Vanessa — can you review the pricing bands and call out any commercial constraints? Karthik/Ben — can you confirm the latency/throughput numbers and whether the fallthrough cache we discussed will need reserved capacity?

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan\Partner GTM / Redwood Inference

Tessa — quick internal note before we send back to Pinecone. Forwarding Jake’s note and your draft attachments.

Key commercial points I want to raise:
- We should avoid a one-size-fits-all revenue split for bundles that incur variable egress; propose a three-band approach: low-touch (no egress), hybrid (S3 fallthrough occasional), high-egress (heavy S3 reads) with minimums for the hybrid/high bands.
- Consider a pilot with capped egress for the first 90 days; simplifies billing and mitigates surprise costs for both sides.
- Need a clause for data residency/geo: if Pinecone requires EU-only storage, add explicit region mapping in SOW.

I updated ops_service_levels.xlsx with suggested SLO rows and a pilot pricing scenario (see tab 'pilot-90d'). Ben — confirm whether we can set a warm-cache size reservation per partner. Karthik — is there tooling to surface per-request egress tags for chargeback?

-Vanessa

We can support a per-partner warm-cache reservation. Operational notes:
- Reservation granularity: 100GB increments, with an API to modify at runtime.
- Warm-cache eviction policy: LRU with token-aware preservation for pinned prefixes (we can pin partner-critical prefixes for the pilot).
- Telemetry: we will return per-request tags that include 'partner_id' and 'egress_bucket' so billing can attribute S3 egress. Those appear in the per-token billing export and are usable by downstream billing pipelines.

Latency: S3 fallthrough median 270ms in our staging tests (cold retrieval path), p90 ~640ms. We can push median down to ~180ms with provisioned warm-cache and a 2x network egress limit (requires reserved capacity).

-I'll add these numbers to the SOW and push back to Jake.
